reader_summary:
I understand the question as: if we train only a small patch of numbers, why does using the result still require the large original model? The book-and-sticky-notes analogy gives the answer: the patch modifies how an existing base behaves; it does not replace all the numbers that the base uses. The chapter starts from a previously trained Qwen image-text base, so its prior capabilities must be distinguished from this course's LoRA changes. A separate Whisper recognizer first turns speech into text; changing that recognizer is a different contribution from changing the image-text base.

The arithmetic estimates only stored weight numbers. The stated 2,127,532,032 parameters each take 4 or 2 bytes, giving about 7.93 or 3.96 GiB. Sixteen-bit storage uses fewer bytes per number, while the number of parameters stays fixed. Runtime picture/conversation work and training state require additional memory. Dense and MoE are presented as different ways to use rules: MoE can select a subset of experts for a position, while their stored weights still count. The exercise substitutes the linked chapter-19 model's 328,128 parameters and then asks why many adjustable numbers alone do not teach natural-picture tasks. I can answer using the training-stage and shrinking-detail prerequisites: suitable checked picture/answer examples and visible detail are also needed.

background_and_links.details: Read the target in full, then the explicitly requested 7.17 and 19.2 and the image-detail link 11.15, and finally reread the full target. 7.17 explains article prediction versus checked assistant examples and a reusable base; 19.2 supplies the 328,128 count and the all-weights versus selected-experts distinction; 11.15 explains why shrinking loses fine detail. Those sections are enough for this target. Their nested prerequisites and external papers are not needed for the arithmetic or written answer, so I did not open them. The TRAINING section-1 link points to actual hardware measurements, which I treated as a cited experiment rather than a necessary step or reproduced evidence.

terminology.details: Parameter is explicitly a stored learned number; 2B is an approximate two-billion label. Bytes-per-number and GiB are supplied numerically, with GiB equal to 1024 cubed bytes. Dense is explained through the absence of expert selection, and the 19.2 workshop explanation gives MoE/expert/router operational meaning. LoRA is introduced at the required level as a small candidate modification; the low-rank mechanism is not needed for this question. Whisper and speech recognizer have the clearly stated dictation role. Gradient and optimizer-state mechanics remain undefined locally; this is a nonblocking terminology note because no exercise calculation requires those mechanics.

examples.details: The original-book / optional-note / dictation-classmate example lets me keep the base, LoRA and recognizer roles separate. The numerical example transparently counts the image-text base alone, excluding additional LoRA and recognizer weights. I personally viewed all three necessary prerequisite figures; their clear labels and visible arrows support the training-stage, expert-storage and detail-loss points. The section does not invite treating the weight multiplication as total measured GPU memory.

program_explanation.details: There is one Python fence. parameters is the stated count of stored base-model numbers. The loop visits two (label, bytes_per_number) pairs: (32-bit, 4) and (16-bit, 2). weight_bytes multiplies that count by the bytes per number. print shows the label and exact bytes, then divides by 1024**3 and rounds to two decimal places for GiB. The underscores in the integer are explained as readability separators. I predicted and then ran the exact arithmetic fence offline with the existing .venv: 32-bit produced 8,510,128,128 bytes and 7.93 GiB; 16-bit produced 4,255,064,064 bytes and 3.96 GiB. No model was loaded or trained. In my own formula W = P*b, P means the parameter count, b bytes per stored number, W weight bytes; W / 1024^3 gives GiB.

exercise.details: The requested single change to 328_128 is identifiable, and 19.2 states where that small-model count comes from. Before execution I predicted 1,312,512 bytes at 32-bit and 656,256 at 16-bit; both GiB displays round to 0.0. The executed exercise matched. The bytes column still demonstrates the large difference, so the rounding surprise is nonblocking and recorded as a note. For the written question I would answer: natural-picture tasks need appropriate pictures paired with desired, checked answers and enough task variety, plus readable detail preserved by image resolution or patches. More adjustable numbers alone cannot recover a stroke lost during shrinking or specify which answer a visible scene should receive. Held-out tasks can check the result, as 7.17 explains.
